thread.title: It's Darkest Before The Dawn For Facebook - Facebook (NASDAQ:FB)

author: Erich Reimer
title: It's Darkest Before The Dawn For Facebook - Facebook (NASDAQ:FB)
text:
The devastating bear market Facebook ( FB ) stock has faced the past few months undoubtedly has led many to wonder whether the company is now collapsing underneath the weight of the variety of regulatory policy, user activity metrics, slowing growth, and increasing operations cost risks that have surfaced for the company this year.
However, I believe the company's downturn is poised for a soon-enough turnaround rather than continuation because the company has weathered a historic hurricane of pressures and threats this past year from governments across the world, the media, and consumers that it has showed extraordinary resiliency to those pressures.
No major competitors seem to have gained ground and even moderate regulatory and policy reactions seem muted. Amid all of this, Facebook in Q3 2018 continued to post growth in Daily Active Users, Monthly Active Users, and historic revenue.
If this is the worst that Facebook can face, then once pressures eventually ease I believe the company seems poised for a historic bounce-back streak.
Facebook In Deep Red Since its high of $217.50 a share on July 25th, the company's stock is down almost 35% in just barely four and a half months, with it having even dipped down further. For a company which had just survived a nightmare public relations scenario in the Cambridge Analytica scandal in the spring, it was a disappointing reversal to hopes the company had moved beyond those worries.
FB data by YCharts
Nonetheless, the sheer negative sentiment on Facebook has been so overwhelming these past few months that it is difficult to imagine it getting any worse. Yet, despite all the regular derisive media reports, such as the recent exposé from The New York Times on Facebook's various internal practices and culture, there has been surprisingly little in terms of actual material changes for Facebook's business environment and operations.
There has been no major competitor arising to challenge Facebook, whether from Apple ( AAPL ), which The New York Times article showed was a particular Facebook enemy, or otherwise. Governments from the United States to Britain to otherwise continue to investigate Facebook, yet there appear to have been little meaningful regulatory or legal mechanisms implemented that actually seriously affect the company's products, user activity, or revenue.
In the meantime, the company continues to grow as Q3 2018 revenue and average revenue per user in the United States hit historic highs. In contrast, operating margin decreased slightly - however, that did not prevent Q3 2018 net income from still hitting a historic level of $5.137 billion with a resulting historic EPS of $1.76.
The fact remains that the underlying secular drivers support increasing use of online communications services for a variety of activities, ranging from business to media to socializing. Facebook and its subsidiary Instagram continue to grab that massive growth with seemingly little that can substantially divert it, as even the unbelievably negative policy and media climate seem to just barely dent Facebook's growth rate, let alone reverse it.
(Source: Facebook Q3 2018 Earnings Presentation )
Undoubtedly, there remain some legitimate financial worries over operating margin and whether Facebook can continue the levels of growth it has experienced in the recent past. It is worth noting too that Facebook's current P/E ratio of roughly 20 isn't even that growth heavy anyway. However, as the Q3 2018 earnings call noted , many of the operating cost increases appear to be investments rather than permanent decreases in operating margin. These investments appear to be in some of the biggest potential drivers of Facebook growth in the future, which include the increasingly popular Facebook Watch as well as potentially other content and subscription services.
In the long-run, these investments more likely will pay off in terms of significant new sources of revenue and earnings for Facebook as compared to a temporary decrease as these services mature.
Conclusion It's a difficult time for Facebook and those with investments in the company. Yet few companies have faced as worse a year on nearly every investment-relevant front, ranging from guidance to policy to media to consumers. Once we push back the noise, we see that the company is still actually doing quite well on all the key fundamentals, ranging from user activity to earnings to investments in future revenue lines, that likely will eventually result in the stock similarly bouncing back once the current negative cloud around the company dissipates.
It seems Facebook itself believes this too, as they just a few days ago added over $9 billion to their stock buyback program. I believe that the company right now is in a value situation and is well-poised to return to and surpass its former levels once all the doom-and-gloom surrounding it right now settles down.
(Source: CNET )
